2607.11020.title: Can a Language Model Learn Facts Continually in Its Weights?
2607.11020.paper_summary: Continual learning promises a language model that keeps acquiring knowledge after training, with each new fact written into its weights. Whether weight writes can support accumulation remains undecided. We follow invented facts written into Qwen3 models from creation through sequences of twenty to one hundred later writes, using held-out questions of five types, with the original model given the fact in its prompt as the reference. Across these experiments, the breadth of the training data determines the kind of knowledge created. Bare-statement training produces recitation, while diverse restatements reduce the recitation-to-use gap from 27.4 to 5.4 points without showing the model a conclusion. This difference carries into later writes: after twenty sequential writes, bare-statement facts retain 1% accuracy while facts written from broad study data retain 46%. We also find that facts can be behaviourally forgotten without being erased. Forgotten facts keep most of the log-probability added by their write, and under bare-statement training 70% of wrong answers about them contain the most recently written fact. The same writes barely degrade the model's use of facts in context, and a forgotten study fact supplied in the prompt recovers to 77-80% on its questions. These results describe knowledge that is stored but question-keyed: later writes redirect the questions that reached it. Damage to unrelated abilities tracks KL divergence from the original model, and the later writes cause interference regardless of how the earlier fact was stored. Broad data can create usable knowledge, and a frozen reference can preserve capability, but no intervention we tested, including those built on accurate local measurements of each write, keeps earlier facts reachable. When facts must be composed or survive later writes, the reliable channel is context rather than the weights.
2607.11020.paper_summary_zh: 持續學習承諾了一種語言模型，該模型在訓練後不斷獲取知識，每個新事實都寫入其權重中。權重的寫入是否能支持積累仍然未決定。我們跟踪從創建到後續二十到一百次寫入的Qwen3模型中的虛構事實，使用五種類型的保留問題，原始模型在提示中提供該事實作為參考。在這些實驗中，訓練數據的廣度決定了所創造的知識類型。單純陳述的訓練產生重述，而多樣的重述則將重述與使用之間的差距從27.4縮小到5.4點，且未向模型展示結論。這一差異延續到後續的寫入：在二十次連續寫入後，單純陳述的事實保持1%的準確率，而來自廣泛研究數據的事實保持46%。我們還發現，事實可以在不被刪除的情況下被行為性遺忘。被遺忘的事實保留了其寫入所增加的大部分對數概率，在單純陳述的訓練下，關於它們的70%的錯誤答案包含最近寫入的事實。這些寫入幾乎不會削弱模型在上下文中使用事實的能力，而在提示中提供的被遺忘的研究事實在其問題上恢復到77-80%。這些結果描述了被存儲但以問題為鍵的知識：後續的寫入重新引導了到達它的問題。對無關能力的損害與原始模型的KL散度相關，而後續的寫入無論早期事實是如何存儲的都會導致干擾。廣泛的數據可以創造可用的知識，而凍結的參考可以保留能力，但我們測試的任何干預，包括基於每次寫入的準確本地測量所建立的干預，都無法保持早期事實的可達性。當事實必須被構成或在後續寫入中存活時，可靠的渠道是上下文而非權重。
2607.11020.author: Charles O'Neill et.al.
